report.executive_summary: This memo independently verifies A's WO-05 decision brief against the trusted source table. All four packages qualify: quality 100, 95, 91 and 88 clear the 80 gate; defects 3, 1, 3 and 5 stay within the limit of 5. With no exclusions, selection reduces to lowest energy: P2 at 15 kWh leads P3 (24), P1 (44) and P4 (64) by 9, 29 and 49 kWh. A's arithmetic, gate screening, ranking and tightened-gate checks all reproduce exactly under recomputation. P4 sits exactly at the defect limit, the table's only boundary case. The recommendation P2 is client-correct under the supplied policy.
report.figure_caption: Proportional energy bars at 4 px per kWh on a 0-70 kWh axis: P2 leads at 15 kWh; P4 flagged at the 5/5 defect limit. Basis: common output/load acceptance test.

recommendation.rationale: P2 qualifies with the fewest defects (1), second-best quality (95) and lowest energy (15 kWh), leading P3 by 9, P1 by 29 and P4 by 49 kWh. It strictly dominates P3 and P4 on every recorded field and survives every tightened gate that admits it. No open question plausibly closes the 9 kWh gap to P3.

sections.body: Recomputing from the trusted table: the quality gate of at least 80 admits all four candidates (P1 100, P2 95, P3 91, P4 88; margins of 20, 15, 11 and 8). The defect gate of at most 5 admits all four (P1 3, P2 1, P3 3, P4 5). P4 is the sole boundary case with zero margin; one additional defect in any re-test would disqualify it. P2 holds the widest defect slack (4 counts) and second-best quality. Because the qualifying set is all four candidates, the lowest-ID tie-break never activates and selection rests entirely on measured energy.
sections.heading: Recomputed Eligibility and Gate Margins

sections.body: All energy figures share one output, load and acceptance-test basis, so direct comparison is valid. Ascending order: P2 15, P3 24, P1 44, P4 64 kWh input per test. Verified leader gaps: 9 kWh to P3, 29 to P1, 49 to P4. P4 consumes about 4.27 times P2's energy for identical specified output. A's stated gaps of 9/29/49 and its 4.3x ratio are arithmetically correct. The closest rival P3 trails by 9 kWh (a 60 percent disadvantage) while carrying more defects (3 vs 1) and lower quality (91 vs 95), so no recorded field favors P3 over P2.
sections.heading: Verified Energy Ranking and Leader Gaps

sections.body: A's sensitivity analysis is correct. A quality gate of 95 leaves P1 and P2 only, with P2 still lowest-energy; at 96 only P1 survives and wins by default. A defect limit of 4 keeps P1, P2 and P3 with P2 still leading; at 2 only P2 survives. Strict dominance holds: P2 beats P3 on quality (95 vs 91), defects (1 vs 3) and energy (15 vs 24), and beats P4 on all three fields. The only candidate beating P2 on any single field is P1 on quality (100 vs 95), which cannot offset a 29 kWh energy deficit.
sections.heading: Robustness Under Tightened Gates

sections.body: Verified facts: the trusted table, the four-candidate qualifying set, the ranking and the gap arithmetic. Open questions: single readings leave repeat-run variance behind the 15 and 24 kWh figures unknown; defect severity, cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified and correctly excluded from ranking. A's prose this round is accurate and its energy bars are proportional on a stated scale; the 0-70 kWh axis is meaningful for these values, unlike some prior-round subfigures. I flag only that P4's zero defect margin deserves explicit mention in any client handover.
